config.install_script:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd /workspace/rails-postgres-bottleneck-lab
trap 'bin/lab down' EXIT
script/setup-dev
config.start_skill:
Use the existing checkout at /workspace/rails-postgres-bottleneck-lab. Tasks are isolated; do not create Git worktrees unless requested. Read AGENTS.md and README.md. All eight educational phases and optional Prometheus/Grafana monitoring are implemented. Do not claim production failover, online resharding, distributed transactions or production cache consistency.

Docker Engine and Compose v2 are required. Run script/setup-dev from the repository root to refresh frozen gems and public-schema baseline migrations. It never seeds original orders or enables their optional index. Ruby/PostgreSQL/k6/Redis/Prometheus/Grafana images are digest-pinned. PgBouncer uses a pinned signed APT package with the system CA provided as a BuildKit secret; do not bypass signatures or TLS verification. The wrapper sets task UID/GID and retains ignored .bundle/gems. Preserve Docker proxy settings and system CA trust.

If cgroups are unavailable, explicitly set PG_CPUS=0, PG_MEMORY=0, SHARD_CPUS=0 and SHARD_MEMORY=0 in ignored .env without overwriting unknown user settings. These disable caps and cannot support isolated capacity claims. On Ubuntu use .env.example and verify enforcement. Named data volumes are durable; do not delete them as routine cleanup.

Ordinary web startup is bin/lab up -d --wait web. Verify real JSON requests, not /up alone. Benchmark environment disables reload and uses an ephemeral signing key, requiring no master.key. Lab endpoints require LAB_EXPERIMENT_ENDPOINTS=1 and are always disabled in production. All profiles use private database/cache ports and loopback-only UI/API ports. Trust authentication and anonymous Viewer monitoring are local teaching configurations, not production auth.

Phase 1: default db:seed creates 10,000 customers/1,000,000 orders. Inspect existing data first; LAB_RESET=1 explicitly replaces only those rows and is forbidden in production. script/experiment baseline|optimized results/new-directory compares the reversible optional index with fixed K6_VUS/K6_DURATION/WARMUP_DURATION. Ordinary setup preserves the missing customer index. Do not dump an optimized live schema over the baseline source.

Phases 2–4: script/experiment-next accepts pool-starved, pool-balanced, db-exhausted, pooled, locks-long and locks-short. It distinguishes Rails checkout timeout, PostgreSQL non-superuser role connection refusal, row lock timeout and SQL cancellation. Expected baseline errors remain unsuccessful requests. PgBouncer has a bounded transaction pool and uncached protocol checks; do not run migrations through it or assume session SET state survives. Lock runs reset only the dedicated counter with traffic stopped and verify its value equals acknowledged successes.

Phases 5–8: script/experiment-advanced accepts cache-off/on, read-primary/replica, partition-heap/fanout/pruned, shard-single/sharded. Default EVENT_COUNT and SHARD_ORDERS are 1,000,000; SHARD_CUSTOMERS defaults to an even 10,000. Native optional connections use separate standby/shard services and are excluded from ordinary database tasks. script/advanced-checks validates actual cache invalidation/TTL/outage fallback, paused-replay stale reads and LSN fences, PostgreSQL standby write rejection, one-versus-twelve partition relations, equal shard data/aggregates and controlled node outage with restoration. Do not pause a shared production standby. Explicit reset flags apply only to the dedicated experiment tables; original orders remain unchanged.

Read each experiment guide before measuring. Cache-aside is eventual and can suffer stale fills, stampedes and failed invalidation. A physical replica fence is cluster/timeline-specific, not cross-shard. Partitions require valid half-open bounds and actual pruning evidence. Shard ownership changes require data migration; fanout failures must never return an incomplete total as complete. Native shard contexts are request/thread scoped. Same logical data and fixed settings are required within a comparison; extra active nodes are extra compute, not a hidden free speedup. All runners share a flock and refuse overlapping workloads or output overwrites. Record only actual measurements with metadata/limitations.

Optional monitoring: script/monitoring results/new-directory provisions the read-only Viewer dashboard and verifies actual Prometheus scrape and Grafana datasource queries. Automated comparison runners stop observers to keep monitoring overhead controlled. Custom metrics are a teaching collector, not a full production exporter/alerting stack. Source archives without Git metadata are supported and explicitly labeled.

Checks: RAILS_ENV=test bin/lab run --rm web bin/rails test; bin/lab run --rm --no-deps web bin/rubocop; bin/lab run --rm --no-deps web bin/rails zeitwerk:check; bin/lab run --rm --no-deps web bin/brakeman --quiet --no-pager --exit-on-warn --exit-on-error; bin/lab run --rm --no-deps web bin/bundler-audit check --update. There is no Node/asset/importmap workflow.

When finished, run bin/lab --profile '*' down unless asked to keep services running; verify docker ps. Preserve data/keys/.env/source and existing user changes. Do not start obsolete standalone rails-lab-db. Source is local/uncommitted/not pushed; real validation artifacts are in experiment validation directories. This proposal is local because the prior backend draft was locked. Publication and fresh-task restoration require independent verification; processes do not survive snapshots.
